title: Android TV Focus, D-pad Navigation, and Media Quality

scout.purpose: Master android tv focus, d-pad navigation, and media quality through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend android tv focus, d-pad navigation, and media quality.

blocks.text: TV is a ten-foot, focus-driven environment. Every actionable control needs visible focus and predictable D-pad reachability; touch assumptions disappear. Compose for TV or supported components provide focus-aware behavior, but dynamic rows, nested scrolling, popups, and restoration still need testing. Content should dominate chrome, text must be readable at distance, and back should move through a clear hierarchy without trapping users. Overscan assumptions are obsolete but safe spacing remains useful.

blocks.text: Media apps coordinate Media3 playback, audio focus, sessions, remote keys, captions, multiple audio tracks, HDR or codecs, network adaptation, and system recommendations. Deep links to live or selected content should avoid unnecessary blocking screens where quality rules require direct playback. Preserve playback position across process death and account change without leaking profiles. Handle controller, gamepad, keyboard, microphone, and accessibility input where relevant. Avoid autoplay that surprises or consumes data.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Test every screen with D-pad only, focus restoration after navigation or list updates, long rows, RTL, text scaling, TalkBack, captions, low bandwidth, playback error, remote key repeat, process death, and cold deep link. Run TV quality guidelines and device matrix for resolutions and codecs. Measure frame pacing and memory with image-heavy rails. A beautiful screenshot is insufficient if focus becomes invisible or unreachable after asynchronous content arrives.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Reordering a loaded content rail without stable identity or focus restoration can strand focus or jump the user to an unrelated item.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Build a D-pad-only media browse and playback journey with stable focus, deep link, captions, errors, process recovery, and TV quality evidence.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What must survive asynchronous TV list updates?
recall.answer: Stable item identity and an intentional focus restoration target so remote navigation remains predictable.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
